title: The fundamental theorem of chronogeometry on the space of hermitian matrices: every bijective coherency preserver of H_2 extends to an affine automorphism
author: Michiya Mori and Peter \v{S}emrl
work: Optimal version of the fundamental theorem of chronogeometry
difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the paper's own deduction of the optimal fundamental theorem of chronogeometry from the authors' classification of standard coherency preservers, and it is not a qualification exercise. With the whole preceding apparatus supplied - the compactification of H_2, the Bloch representation, Theorem A on standard coherency preservers of H_2, the identity-type theorem, and the unitary Proposition 4.1 - the author still has to run a source-local argument: transport the rank distance d(A,B) = rank(A-B) through the bijection to get phi(H_2^2) = H_2^2; prove the characterisation of H_2^{++} union H_2^{--} by the existence of a coherent point on each line through zero, with the separate trace computation for A in H_2^{++} and the null-vector argument via tr(A^{-1}Q) = 0 for A in H_2^{+-}; use the openness and connectedness of H_2^{++} and H_2^{--} with the path lemma to show that phi either preserves or interchanges them; deduce from the position of -I, 0, I that the triple phi(-I), phi(0), phi(I) is timelike, extend phi to an automorphism of the compactification by Theorem A, and finally identify the extension as affine by conjugating with the automorphism X -> X^{-1} - I, applying the unitary proposition on [0,I] and propagating the resulting equality to the whole compactification by the identity-type theorem. Every one of those steps is carried by the paper's own theory of coherency preservers rather than by quoting a textbook, which places the unit well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in geometry or operator theory.
